as_told.title: Chemical analysis of the Giza iron veins

plain: The claim is that the bedrock beneath the pyramids at Giza in Egypt is laced with veins of iron ore that also hold precious metals and rare earth elements, a group of metals used in modern electronics. The researcher Jeffrey Drum (whose name also appears as Geoffrey Drumm) argues that the pyramids were built as machines for making energy. He tells Michels there is 'chemical analysis data from these iron veins,' mineral deposits left by hot water and 'embedded in the bedrock,' that are 'permeated with rare earth elements, gold, silver.' Later in the same interview he says the samples 'also contain gold, silver, electrum,' a natural mix of gold and silver, 'everything that you could think of.' In a later episode he speaks only of 'valuable metal deposits.' He does not say who did the analysis. The story's title adds platinum, but none of the quoted words name it. For Drum, the metals in the rock help explain why the pyramids were built where they are.
